chunks: Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad narrated to me, saying: Ibn Mu'az narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn al-Marwazi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ubayd narrated to us, saying: Dawud al-Awadi narrated from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family).

He said: 'The first thing by which people from my nation enter Hell are the two cavities.' They asked: 'O Messenger of God, what are the two cavities?' He replied: 'The stomach and the mouth.' And the most common thing by which people enter Paradise is God-consciousness and good character.

key_terms.الْأَجْوَفَانِ: The two cavities (referring to stomach and mouth)

ai.seo_question: What are the two main causes of entering Hell and Paradise according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq presents this hadith to illustrate the microcosmic relationship between the body's primary orifices and spiritual destiny, a concept deeply rooted in Shia ethical theology. While the 'two cavities' (stomach and mouth) are identified as the gateways to Hell through unchecked consumption and speech, the hadith elevates *taqwa* and *husn al-khuluq* as the transformative virtues that ensure entry into Paradise, linking physical discipline directly to moral character.
